title: Identity contract packaging pilot: observable SSO/SAML and RBAC commitments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Run a small controlled experiment to validate two packaging approaches for enterprise customers who require SSO/SAML and role-based access controls (RBAC) as contract commitments. Goal: determine which packaging minimizes sales friction, limits legal risk, and produces predictable operational commitments for Dedicated and Private deployments. Two variants: (A) Compliance Addendum — a detachable legal addendum that enumerates SSO/SAML integration SLAs, RBAC mapping responsibilities, and audit log retention commitments; (B) Embedded Identity Tier — a product tier where SSO/SAML and granular RBAC are included in the product price and tied to entitlement gating. This ticket coordinates drafting contract language, legal & security reviews, pilot customer selection, and metrics instrumentation to measure sales cycle impact, support load, and upgrade/downgrade friction.
acceptance_criteria: Drafted and reviewed contract clauses for both packaging variants (legal + security sign-off)
Clear operational commitments defined (onboarding runbook, SLOs for identity onboarding, KB for integration)
Pilot with at least three enterprise prospects (one current pipeline, two sourced by AE) executed and feedback captured
Telemetry: tracked time-to-close, contract negotiation touchpoints, and support tickets related to identity for pilot customers
Decision memo produced recommending one packaging approach with quantified trade-offs and follow-up rollout plan
comments: 2025-02-12: Kickoff with GTM, Legal, Security, Solutions Eng. Agreed scope: only SSO/SAML + RBAC commitments; MFA, SCIM and advanced cert tooling deferred.
2025-02-18: Legal flagged risk around rigid SLAs for identity onboarding — added fallback language and measurable acceptance criteria instead of hard uptime SLAs.
2025-02-24: Solutions Eng requested an onboarding runbook and an engineer-hours estimate per customer for the Embedded Identity Tier; estimate ~24-40hrs for first-time integrations.

2025-02-28: Sales shared three customer prospects willing to pilot: Acme Fintech (high compliance), Boxwell Health (PHI scope), and NovaRetail (mid-market platform). Preparing pilot consent and NDA addendum.
2025-03-02: Design reviewed UI gating patterns for entitlement controls in console; mockups to be uploaded to Drive.
2025-03-04: Security requested encryption-at-rest and KMS mapping to be explicitly called out in Compliance Addendum — added as sub-clause.
Ongoing: tracking negotiation threads with AEs in shared spreadsheet and capturing redlines for iterative clause improvement.
decisions: Pilot will run with both packaging variants in parallel across the three customers to compare sales friction and engineering effort.
We will not commit to SLA penalties in pilot contracts; instead use remediation and escalation pathways with specified response windows.
Embedded Identity Tier will include a documented onboarding credit (one free integration cycle) to reduce time-to-value and make comparison with Compliance Addendum clearer.
risks: If pilot customers produce widely different legal redlines, a single packaging approach may not scale and will require more granular contractual options.
Operational risk: underestimating integration effort could create support overload if multiple pilots overlap; we need clear engineering reservation policies.
Financial risk: including identity in a priced tier may compress margins if engineering hours per customer are high and not amortized by pricing.
